experiment: Resolve callee bindings once during free-variable analysis
hypothesis: Direct-call analysis repeats local, enclosing and global binding searches in the builtin skip and name collector. Resolving bindings once can reduce executed instructions without changing capture results.
correctness_counterexamples: Local bindings precede enclosing locals, which precede globals and builtin skipping
Only capture callees skip inline builtins; reads, writes and used-builtin queries preserve names
Skipped callees still traverse every argument
Throw payload handling and self-reference collisions retain their prior semantics

candidate_bump.changes: Consolidate callee binding lookup in common_analysis.vibe

candidate_rc.changes: Consolidate callee binding lookup in common_analysis.vibe

callee_scan_fuel.description: 100 free-variable queries over 256 direct global calls, 16 local parameter names; setup included; linear RC target
callee_scan_fuel.note: Both probe binaries were compiled by the same baseline compiler before and after the implementation change. Fuel is Wasmtime executed-instruction cost, not native instructions or wall time.

profiles.note: Separate diagnostic runs, not uninstrumented wall-time samples; both compilers read the final source snapshot.

interpretation: The comparison is a pure compiler implementation change: every generated target is byte-identical across compilers, temperatures and rounds. Heap-pointer, linear capacity and RSS are distinct metrics. Wall-time spread and the A/A control limit the precision of timing claims.
